Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used as shell commands.
- Most bash commands should end with a newline (\n) to cause them to execute
- For special key sequences, use: C-c for Ctrl+C, C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies wait time:
- 0.1 seconds for instant commands (cd, ls, echo, cat)
- 1.0 seconds for normal commands (gcc, find, rustc)
- 5-30 seconds for slow commands (make, python scripts, wget)

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are executed in sequence
- Do not include extra whitespace unless it's part of the command
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action
- Set task_complete to true ONLY when the task is fully finished and verified
- CRITICAL: BEFORE writing any code or modifying files, you MUST explore the workspace and read the provided documentation (e.g., `cat skill.md` or `cat task_spec.json`) to learn the required skills and constraints.

## Overview
A revenue model is not just "how much do I charge" — it is the complete system of how value translates into money. The wrong model can make a great product fail (people love it but won't pay the way you structured it). The right model turns a good product into a sustainable business. This playbook helps you choose, design, and validate the right model for your specific situation.

---

## Step 1: Understand the Revenue Model Landscape

Know your options before choosing. Each model has different implications for cash flow, customer behavior, product design, and growth.

### Recurring Revenue Models
Money comes in on a predictable schedule. The backbone of sustainable solopreneur businesses.

- Cons: Churn is constant. Must continuously deliver value or people cancel.
- Best for: SaaS products, tools, services with ongoing value delivery.

# Revenue Model Design: Invoice Follow-Up Automation SaaS

## Executive Summary

**Product:** B2B SaaS tool for invoice follow-up automation  
**Target:** Freelance accountants and tiny agencies (1-10 person teams)  
**Goal:** Predictable monthly revenue with minimal billing complexity  

---

## 1. Primary Revenue Model: Tiered Subscription

### Recommendation: Monthly SaaS Subscription

**Why this fits:**
- Matches the business goal of predictable recurring revenue
- Aligns with how the product delivers value (ongoing automation)
- Customers mentally amortize cost (feels cheaper than one-time)
- Compounds over time as you add customers

### Pricing Tiers

| Tier | Price/Month | Best For | Key Features |
|------|-------------|----------|-------------|
| Starter | $29 | Solo freelancers | Up to 50 invoices/mo, basic reminders, 1 user |
| Pro | $79 | Small agencies | Up to 200 invoices/mo, custom templates, 3 users, API access |
| Agency | $149 | Growing teams | Unlimited invoices, white-label, 10 users, priority support |

**Pricing Rationale:**
- Entry point ($29) is low-risk for freelancers to try
- Pro tier ($79) targets the sweet spot for small agencies
- Agency tier ($149) captures larger teams willing to pay for scale

---

## 2. Secondary Revenue Stream: Template Pack

### One-Time Digital Product: Invoice Template Library

**Product:** Pre-built email templates for different scenarios (friendly reminder, final notice, payment received, etc.)

**Price:** $49 one-time (or free for Pro+ subscribers)

**Why this works:**
- Low marginal cost (create once, sell repeatedly)
- Serves customers who want customization before committing to subscription
- Can be upsell to existing free trial users
- Builds brand authority in the niche

**Distribution:**
- Standalone purchase via landing page
- Included free in Pro/Agency tiers (increases perceived value)
- Upsell offer during checkout for Starter tier

---

## 3. Opportunistic Revenue: Setup Consulting

### Productized Service: Onboarding Setup Call

**Price:** $199 one-time (or free for Agency tier)

**Scope:**
- 60-minute video call
- Walk through invoice import from their existing system
- Configure reminder schedules and templates
- Train their team on the platform

**Why keep this optional:**
- High-touch service that doesn't scale well
- Can be productized (fixed scope, fixed price)
- Agency tier customers get this free (increases conversion)
- Can be outsourced to a VA as you grow

---

## 4. Payment Flow Design

### Primary Stream: SaaS Subscription

```
REVENUE STREAM: SaaS Subscription

## 7. Risk Mitigation

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|------------|
| High churn | Focus on onboarding, add in-app tutorials, check-in emails |
| Low conversion | A/B test pricing page, add social proof, offer money-back guarantee |
| Payment failures | Implement dunning management, retry logic, multiple payment methods |
| Feature creep | Stick to core value prop, defer nice-to-haves, gather customer input |

## 8. Tools Stack (Solo Founder Optimized)

- **Payments:** Stripe (handles subscriptions, one-time, invoices)
- **Website:** Next.js + Vercel (free tier sufficient initially)
- **Email:** ConvertKit or MailerLite (free up to 1,000 subscribers)
- **Analytics:** PostHog or Plausible (privacy-friendly, affordable)
- **Support:** Crisp or Tally (free tier for chat/forms)
- **Calendar:** Calendly (free tier for consulting bookings)

## Final Recommendation

**Start with the subscription model as your core.** It provides the predictable revenue you need while aligning with how your product delivers ongoing value. Add the template pack early as a low-effort secondary stream. Keep consulting optional and productized to avoid becoming a bottleneck.

**Don't overcomplicate billing.** Stripe handles 95% of what you need. Add annual plans and more complex features only after you have traction.

**Focus on reducing churn.** For a solo founder, retaining existing customers is cheaper and easier than acquiring new ones. Invest in onboarding and customer success.
